annotationRationale: Coprimality rules out interior lattice points on the diagonal, allowing the horizontal and vertical crossing counts to be added without overlap.
sourceMethod: Follows the official edge-crossing count, adding a coordinate explanation of why relatively prime side lengths prevent simultaneous crossings.

review.mathCheck: An interior tile corner would satisfy 17y=10x, forcing 17 to divide x, impossible for 0<x<17. Thus the 16 vertical and 9 horizontal crossings are distinct. The monotone path visits 1+25=26 tiles, choice C, including both endpoint tiles.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 10 on page 5: exclude interior corner crossings, then count edge crossings plus the starting tile. The supplied grid figure agrees.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed lattice restrictions and disjoint addition match the work; GCF is appropriate supporting knowledge. No material omission.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact addition-principle and GCF links support the named steps. The coprimality divisibility argument extends beyond merely finding a GCF; lattice counting has no supplied national link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The accepted partial 6.NS.B.4 link supports recognizing GCF(10,17)=1 within its bounds. This problem does not demonstrate its LCM or distributive-property components, and that link does not cover the lattice divisibility argument.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All three nodes fit: math:lattice-counting rules out interior integer points, cnm_h230 combines disjoint crossings, and cnm_p158 supplies background coprimality.
